jobs.description:
Job Description Summary:

Role Type: Individual Contributor
Primary Location: Tokyo, Japan

At The Coca Cola Company, our ambition is to refresh the world and make a difference, and finance plays a critical role in bringing that vision to life. As part of our Finance Hub, the FP&A Supply Chain Corporate team ensures the integrity, transparency, and efficiency of key financial processes that enable the entire system to thrive. In this role, you will contribute to accurate product costing and pricing processes, delivering insights that support innovation and operational excellence across multiple regions. By leveraging your analytical expertise and digital fluency, you will help optimize supply chain transparency, standardize processes, and build efficiencies that support growth across emerging and established markets. If you are passionate about finance, technology, and improving global processes in a collaborative and forward-thinking organization, this is your opportunity to make a meaningful impact within one of the world’s most recognized brands.

What You will do for us
- Prepare, release, and maintain product standard costs and related SAP master data for new product launches or reformulations for assigned plant locations, ensuring accurate and timely communication to stakeholders.
- Execute re‑costing of materials based on Bill of Material changes, analyzing cost impacts and validating results for assigned plants.
- Lead Pricing and Purchase Price Variance (PPV) processes for assigned locations, collaborating with stakeholders to ensure pricing compliance and accuracy.
- Oversee daily deliverables from third‑party service providers for pricing and accounting tasks, validating work against internal controls and corrective action standards.
- Serve as the primary point of contact for costing and pricing escalations, applying a broad perspective to resolve complex issues.
- Coordinate internal and external audit requirements relating to costing, revenue, and volume reporting, maintaining proper documentation and compliance standards.
- Promote consistent application of global standards and best practices in cost and pricing management, partnering with regional teams for continuous improvements.
- Reconcile and monitor Cost of Goods Sold clearing account balances for timely recognition of financial results.
- Drive process optimization by identifying opportunities for enhancement, preparing performance metrics, and facilitating alignment across teams.
- Act as finance subject‑matter contributor on global initiatives such as S/4HANA deployments and other supply chain transformations, ensuring finance requirements are effectively represented.

Requirements and Qualifications
- Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, or related field; equivalent practical experience accepted.
- Minimum of 5 years’ progressive experience in finance, accounting, or supply chain costing roles.
- Professional accounting designation (CIMA, ACCA, or equivalent) preferred.
- Proven proficiency in SAP or similar integrated manufacturing systems.
- Strong digital and data literacy, including the ability to leverage analytics for decision support and process efficiency.
- Fluency in English; Additional languages such as Japanese is preferred.
- Ability to build strong relationships with internal stakeholders and manage external service provider performance.
- Demonstrated growth mindset with experience in driving process improvements and embracing transformation initiatives.
- Skilled in managing competing priorities, analyzing complex data, and applying problem‑solving to supply chain challenges.

What We’ll Do for You
- Enable you to work on regional and global initiatives that directly support Coca‑Cola’s supply chain and operational strategies.
- Provide exposure to digital transformation projects that shape how finance operates globally, expanding your technical capabilities.
- Offer robust development opportunities including mentorship, cross‑market collaboration, and access to the company’s learning platforms.
- Connect you with a dynamic and diverse team focused on continuous improvement, innovation, and process standardization.

jobs.title: Senior Director, General Manager, Tea Company
jobs.description:
Job Description Summary:

The Coca-Cola Company, a global beverage leader with a rich history of 140 years and a portfolio of over 200 brands worldwide and TeaCo is a dedicated 'hothouse' tasked with step-change growth and disruptive innovation in the ready-to-drink tea category. Operating within a 'sandbox' (primarily Guangdong province, with initial focus on the Greater Guangzhou area), TeaCo is expected to:

•    Test creative ideas and new business models at startup speed.
•    Leverage the global scale of Coca-Cola and local execution strength of Swire
•    Deliver validated concepts that can scale back into the core ATH system or launch as independent brands.
•    Achieve +150M incremental unit cases over a 3-year horizon.

This is not a traditional internal functional leadership role. It requires entrepreneurial capability, commercial ownership, stakeholder management, and the ability to operate in ambiguity with pace. The position is legally hosted under Coca-Cola, reporting to the Synthetic Board, within a virtual entity structure where costs are shared proportionally between KO and Swire.

What You'll Do for Us:

Own the Innovation Agenda and Product Roadmap
•   Define the innovation strategy, prioritize concepts, and manage the pipeline from ideation to pilot launch
•   Lead consumer insight integration, concept development, and rapid prototyping
•   Ensure innovation efforts protect and enhance the ATH master brand equity
•    Build and test digitally enabled commercialization models, including digital consumer acquisition, O2O activation, DTC experimentation, social commerce, and platform partnerships.

Own Commercial and Financial Outcomes
•   Full P&L ownership for TeaCo — accountable for revenue, cost, margin, and investment returns
•    Build and refine the business model across incubation, early commercialization, and potential scale phases
•    Deliver against +150M unit cases 3-year target

Build and Lead a High-Performance, Lean Team
•    Recruit, develop, and retain a world-class, entrepreneurial team (1+4 structure).
•    Foster a culture of speed, experimentation, accountability, and psychological safety.
•    Attract talent willing to embrace a 60%+ failure rate on individual experiments (as a portfolio, the goal is success).

Manage Complex Stakeholder Ecosystem
•    Internal: Navigate Coca-Cola (Shanghai HQ, GDI (Global Development and Innovation), Consumer Insights, KO Legal), Swire (TAC, S&M, Supply Chain), and XNode (external facilitator).
•    External: Co-packers, ingredient suppliers, research agencies, advisory network.
•    Governance: Manage Board engagement, prepare for Gate Reviews, and ensure transparent progress reporting

Drive Speed-to-Market and Consumer Validation
•   Move from concept to consumer test in 90-day cycles where possible.
•    Build rapid feedback loops with target consumers in the Guangzhou test market.
•    Make "accelerate/ pivot/ pause/ stop" decisions with confidence and data.
•    Use digital channels and consumer data to test propositions, acquire target consumers, and accelerate product-market fit validation.

jobs.title: Senior Director, Vendor Management & Governance Lead
jobs.description:
Job Description Summary:

At The Coca-Cola Company, our purpose is to refresh the world and make a difference. We bring this purpose to life by creating loved brands, operating sustainably, and building a better shared future for people, communities, and the planet. Our culture is grounded in curiosity, empowerment, inclusion, agility, and doing the right thing—beliefs that inspire us to act with courage, collaborate across boundaries, and create meaningful, lasting impact.

We are seeking a Senior Director, Vendor Management, Governance & Contract Lifecycle Management who will provide strategic leadership and enterprise-wide direction for the organization’s technology vendor ecosystem, with responsibility for establishing and advancing a scalable global governance model across all technology vendors and strategic partnerships, governing the technology supplier ecosystem supporting enterprise infrastructure and services, and leading the Contract Lifecycle Management platform that houses and governs indirect purchasing contracts and vendor accounts.

This role serves as a senior advisor to technology and business leadership, shaping vendor strategy, commercial governance, supplier performance, third-party risk, financial optimization, and strategic sourcing. The Senior Director partners across IT, Procurement, Finance, Legal, Risk, and business functions to ensure external technology partnerships deliver measurable business value, innovation, operational resilience, cost optimization, and sustainable competitive advantage.

The position leads the evolution of vendor relationships from traditional service-provider arrangements into strategic partnerships focused on business outcomes, continuous improvement, innovation, and long-term enterprise value.

What You’ll Do for Us
Vendor Governance Strategy & Leadership
- Evolve and expand the work of the current global IT Vendor Governance program and team to further maximize vendor performance, strengthen strategic supplier relationships, and drive measurable business outcomes aligned with enterprise technology and organizational objectives. Set the multiyear strategy, transformation roadmap, investment priorities, and success measures for vendor governance, supplier performance, and commercial management.
- Build, lead, coach, and develop a high-performing team, establishing clear accountabilities, succession plans, and professional development priorities.
- Establish multiyear governance frameworks, operating models, policies, and standards covering vendor selection, onboarding, contracting, performance management, risk management, financial governance, and relationship management.
- Define supplier segmentation and tiering models, including appropriate governance requirements, benefits, incentives, performance expectations, and engagement models.
- Establish executive governance forums and decision-making mechanisms that enable timely escalation, enterprise prioritization, and accountability for financial, operational, service, and risk outcomes.
- Continuously mature the vendor governance program using business-partner feedback, performance data, market intelligence, industry trends, and leading practices.
- Serve as a strategic advisor to IT leadership and business stakeholders on vendor strategy, supplier performance, commercial opportunities, and third-party risk.

Contract, Financial & Commercial Management
- Provide financial and commercial governance (e.g. budgeting, forecasting, purchase orders)  across the technology supplier portfolio in close partnership with Procurement, Legal, Finance, Global Digital Network, Digital Transformation Office , and business stakeholders.
- Identify opportunities for contract consolidation, optimization, volume discounts, improved commercial terms, and cost avoidance while maintaining required service levels, business continuity, and strategic outcomes.
- Develop strategic supplier relationships that extend beyond transactional contract management and support innovation and long-term enterprise objectives.

- Monitor supplier billing and contractual financial commitments, resolving discrepancies and ensuring appropriate financial controls.
- Develop data-driven reporting that provides leadership with visibility into supplier spend, savings, forecasts, contractual obligations, and commercial opportunities, including but not limited to dashboards, Vendor Performance Scorecards, and Vendor Risk Management reporting.

Contract Lifecycle Management Strategy & Operations
- Continue to support the Legal Functions digitization and technology transformation to develop and own an enterprise CLM strategy, operating model, governance framework, and multiyear roadmap aligned with business, technology, procurement, legal, financial, and risk priorities.
- Lead the evaluation, selection, design, configuration, implementation, integration, and continuous enhancement of the CLM platform, workflows, templates, controls, and reporting capabilities.
- Assist the Legal function in establishing standardized processes across the full contract lifecycle, including intake, drafting, review, negotiation, approval, execution, storage, amendments, renewals, obligations, and termination.
- Implement the defined CLM policies, decision rights, approval thresholds, service levels, data standards, and accountability across Procurement, Legal, Finance, IT, Risk, and business functions.
- Lead stakeholder engagement, communications, training, change management, and user support to drive enterprise adoption and sustained process compliance.
- Implement dashboards and performance measures that provide visibility into contract volumes, cycle times, upcoming renewals, obligations, compliance, value realization, and contractual risk.
- Lead CLM program governance, platform support, data quality, access management, process optimization, and continuous improvement.
- Evaluate and implement opportunities to use automation, analytics, and artificial intelligence to improve contract review, obligation management, risk identification, and decision-making.

Vendor Performance & Continuous Improvement
- Establish standardized vendor KPIs, SLAs, customer satisfaction measures, scorecards, and performance-management methodologies.
- Lead Monthly, Quarterly, and Annual Business Reviews with strategic suppliers to assess performance, address service gaps, identify improvement opportunities, and align on future priorities.
- Use performance analytics and stakeholder feedback to identify trends, improve supplier accountability, and drive measurable continuous improvement.
- Develop corrective-action and improvement plans for underperforming suppliers and monitor progress against agreed commitments.

Third-Party Risk & Compliance
- Integrate vendor risk management into the overall governance framework, including contractual, operational, financial, security, privacy, and compliance considerations.
- Partner with appropriate risk, security, legal, and compliance teams to ensure supplier relationships meet organizational and regulatory requirements, including GDPR and SOX.
- Establish mechanisms for identifying, monitoring, escalating, and mitigating vendor-related risks throughout the supplier lifecycle.
- Ensure governance processes provide appropriate documentation, transparency, accountability, and audit readiness.
- Maintain transparent reporting of the scale and health of the vendor and contract portfolio—including supplier spend, strategic-vendor coverage, contract volumes, geographic reach, team capacity, and risk exposure—to support executive decisions and resource prioritization.

Stakeholder & Supplier Relationship Management
- Build strong relationships with senior IT leaders, Procurement, Legal, Finance, DTO Counterparts, business stakeholders, and strategic suppliers.
- Serve as a primary point of leadership for key supplier relationships, balancing service performance, financial value, innovation, risk, and business priorities.
- Enhance stakeholder and supplier engagement by establishing transparent governance, clear performance expectations, and consistent communication.
- Facilitate resolution of complex vendor issues requiring coordination across multiple internal and external stakeholders.

Innovation & Strategic Partnerships
- Create programs that encourage technology partners to contribute innovative ideas, capabilities, and solutions to the organization.
- Develop supplier recognition and engagement initiatives that reinforce innovation, collaboration, and measurable business value.
- Lead enterprise technology recognition initiatives, including global programs that identify and celebrate innovative technology solutions across the broader ecosystem.

Required Qualifications
- Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain Management, Business Administration, or a related field.
- 10+ years of experience in Vendor Management, Supplier Management, Strategic Sourcing, Procurement, Technology Operations, or a related discipline.
- Demonstrated experience designing and implementing enterprise or global vendor governance programs.
- Strong experience managing large technology supplier portfolios and complex managed-services relationships.
- Proven track record of leading complex, cross-functional initiatives from planning through execution and value realization.
- Proven expertise in contract negotiation, strategic sourcing, commercial management, supplier performance, and financial governance.
- Experience developing vendor KPIs, SLAs, scorecards, dashboards, business reviews, and performance improvement plans.
- Strong understanding of third-party risk, regulatory compliance, and governance requirements, including GDPR and SOX.
- Experience working cross-functionally with senior stakeholders across IT, Procurement, Legal, Finance, Risk, and business organizations.
- Exceptional negotiation, executive communication, relationship management, analytical, and problem-solving skills.
- Strong financial acumen with experience managing budgets, forecasts, supplier spend, savings initiatives, and commercial commitments.

Preferred Qualifications
- Advanced degree in Business Administration, Supply Chain Management, Technology Management, or a related field.
- Demonstrated experience leading an enterprise CLM transformation and end-to-end implementation of a major CLM platform, including process design, integrations, data migration, governance, deployment, and post-launch optimization.
- Demonstrated experience leading organizational change and driving adoption across Procurement, Legal, Finance, IT, Risk, and business teams.
- Experience managing global technology suppliers and complex, multinational stakeholder environments.
- Relevant certification in procurement, sourcing, contract management, vendor management, change management, or project management.

Core Capabilities
- Strategic Execution & Value Delivery
Ability to translate enterprise strategy into actionable execution plans and consistently deliver measurable business outcomes. Drives disciplined execution across complex, cross-functional initiatives with a clear focus on value realization.
- Governance & Operating Model Excellence
Designs and implements effective governance structures, decision frameworks, and operating rhythms that enhance transparency, accountability, and execution consistency across initiatives.
- Performance Management & Value Realization
Defines success metrics, monitors performance, and ensures initiatives deliver against expected value through robust tracking, reporting, and continuous recalibration of priorities.
- Enterprise Prioritization & Resource Optimization
Evaluates competing priorities, balances resource allocation, and aligns organizational capacity to maximize impact and ensure focus on the highest-value initiatives.
- Stakeholder Leadership & Influence
Builds strong, trust-based relationships across functions and levels, aligning diverse stakeholders and influencing outcomes in a matrixed environment without direct authority.
- Data, Digital & Artificial Intelligence Fluency

The Senior Manager, Sales – Walmart drives growth across Coca‑Cola’s beverage portfolio by developing collaborative, data‑driven strategies that strengthen category performance both in-store and online.

This role combines customer leadership, insight application, and cross‑functional collaboration to deliver omnichannel success across Walmart’s extensive retail ecosystem. The ideal candidate will bring proven experience in account management, e-commerce strategy, and joint business planning within consumer goods, translating insights into commercially executable plans. Working closely with merchants across beverage categories, Coca‑Cola brand leaders, and bottling partners, you will help shape the future of how our brands connect with shoppers wherever they choose to purchase.

Job Description Summary:

The Senior IT Procurement Director is a key member of the IT Procurement leadership team and is an individual contributor. The role partners closely with Global Technology, Digital Services, Cyber Security, Finance, Legal, and operating-unit leaders to enable Coca‑Cola’s digital and technology transformation agenda while ensuring governance, compliance, and measurable strategic value. We are looking for a proactive leader who is comfortable operating in a matrix, builds strong internal and supplier relationships, leads with integrity and inclusion, brings excellent negotiation skills, and delivers results through disciplined execution.

The position oversees category strategy development and execution, strategic sourcing, negotiations, contracting, and supplier relationship management for specific IT products and services categories. It also serves as a trusted advisor to business partners and contributes to strategy and policy guidance to ensure the cost-effective flow of IT products and services across the organization. In addition, the role manages relationships with strategic IT suppliers within certain categories to secure favorable terms, mitigate risk, and identify innovations that support business objectives. Recognized as an expert both internally and externally, this leader partners with senior IT executives to evaluate new supplier and technology requests, recommend approvals or rejections, and continuously refine IT procurement strategies. The role is responsible for delivering value, optimizing costs, maintaining supplier quality and compliance, managing supply risk, shaping policy recommendations, fostering innovation, and aligning procurement strategies with broader business goals.

Key Responsibilities:

Own Global IT Sub-Category Strategy
- Develop and execute sub-category strategies for digital technology services. This could include sub-categories such as IT professional services, cloud, infrastructure, application services and enterprise software.
- Lead end‑to‑end sourcing initiatives, including RFIs, RFPs, negotiations, supplier selection, and contract execution.
- Drive total cost of ownership (TCO) optimization, cost avoidance, and working‑capital improvements across the technology portfolio.

Lead Strategic Supplier Relationships
- Build long‑term, trust‑based partnerships with strategic technology and software suppliers; position Coca‑Cola as a customer of choice through transparency and mutual respect.
- Co-create roadmaps with suppliers to drive transformation, innovation, and outcome‑based delivery models.
- Align internal stakeholders and suppliers through change; manage risk and ensure continuity while maintaining flexible relationships.

- Provide commercial leadership for large‑scale technology programs, transformations, and renewals.
